comparison: Perfect agreement on C26-C28. Both evaluations find the behavioral data (seizure recovery vs. crawling velocity) well-supported and accept the interpretation of altered network robustness without functional impairment. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Perfect agreement on C31-C33. Both evaluations accept the GCaMP imaging data showing increased synchronicity and its link to seizure phenotype. Both rate as SUPPORTED without concerns.

Strong agreement on C37-C43 regarding E:I imbalance. Both evaluations endorse the electrophysiology showing differential changes in excitation vs. inhibition. Peer review calls this 'a major accomplishment' and OpenEval confirms statistical support. Both rate as SUPPORTED. Note: Peer R3 includes C36, C38, C41 which OpenEval addresses separately in R11.

Partial overlap on baseline measurements (C36, C38, C41). OpenEval notes uncertainty about C36 interpretation (baseline firing difference), while peer review accepts these as part of the broader electrophysiology findings without specific concern. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with caveats; peer review includes in broader SUPPORTED evaluation.

Agreement on postsynaptic mechanism (C46-C48). Both evaluations accept the voltage-clamp data showing amplitude but not frequency changes. Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer R4 also includes Sr2+ data (C51-C54) which OpenEval addresses separately in R5.

Agreement on Sr2+ validation of postsynaptic mechanism (C51-C54). Both evaluations strongly endorse this technical approach and findings. Peer review highlights this as a specific strength. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on morphological findings (C55-C58). Both evaluations accept the confocal data showing no structural changes. OpenEval notes C58 is speculative about receptor changes; peer review acknowledges molecular mechanism remains unknown but finds discussion adequate. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on CP temporal specificity (C60-C63). Both evaluations accept the 17-19hr AEL window validation. However, peer review requests additional controls (L1/L2 exposure experiments) to strengthen CP specificity claims. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED; peer review rates SUPPORTED but with request for additional validation.

Divergence on rescue interpretation (C64-C70). OpenEval finds rescue experiments strongly support the integration hypothesis (SUPPORTED). Peer review acknowledges rescue is demonstrated but expresses concerns about mechanistic interpretation, noting experiments are 'somewhat difficult to interpret' due to unclear specificity and potential secondary adaptations (UNCERTAIN).

Agreement on dose-dependent effects (C73-C75). Both evaluations accept the graded rescue with different sound intensities. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED; peer review accepts findings as demonstrating dose-dependence (SUPPORTED), though mechanistic interpretation shares uncertainties noted for PTX rescue.

Agreement on bidirectional effects at 21°C (C76-C80). Both evaluations accept the data showing reduced baseline seizures and bidirectional effects of stimulation. OpenEval finds this strongly supports integration hypothesis (SUPPORTED); peer review accepts as demonstrating generalizability (SUPPORTED).

Agreement on Sr2+ technique validation (C49-C50). Both evaluations accept this as established methodology properly validated. Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer R12 groups this with other methodological claims not specifically evaluated by OpenEval.

Agreement on background/context claims (C1-C3, C11-C16). Both evaluations accept these as well-established concepts appropriately cited. Both rate as SUPPORTED. These provide context rather than novel findings.

Agreement on CP mechanism synthesis (C81-C87). Both evaluations accept these claims as accurate representation of prior literature and current contribution. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED; peer review accepts as appropriate contextualization (SUPPORTED).

Agreement on speculative nature of set point hypothesis (C98-C104). OpenEval explicitly rates as UNCERTAIN, noting claims are speculative. Peer review accepts discussion as appropriate contextualization, acknowledging molecular mechanisms remain unknown but finding discussion adequate (SUPPORTED as discussion, not as proven claims).

Agreement on speculative mechanisms (C92-C97). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting explicit speculation and need for further experiments. Peer review accepts as reasonable discussion of unknowns (SUPPORTED as appropriate discussion framework).

Agreement on molecular mechanism speculation (C105-C111). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN since pathways not directly tested. Peer review accepts discussion as adequate contextualization (SUPPORTED as discussion). Both acknowledge these are plausible but untested candidates.

Agreement on speculative rescue mechanisms (C115-C124). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting multiple speculative interpretations requiring validation. Peer review accepts as reasonable interpretation within discussion context (SUPPORTED as interpretive framework).

Agreement on CP integration synthesis (C125-C130). OpenEval finds this supported by dose-dependent rescue and prior literature (SUPPORTED). Peer review endorses this interpretive framework as reasonable (SUPPORTED).
Agreement on prior work citation (C131-C132). Both evaluations accept these as appropriate references to support broader concepts. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on main conclusions (C133-C137). Both evaluations endorse these summary claims as well-supported by experimental data. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED; peer review endorses overall interpretive framework (SUPPORTED).

Peer review provides overarching endorsement of core findings (C4-C10) about CP tuning of network excitability. This represents editorial/reviewer synthesis not specifically evaluated as a separate result by OpenEval, though the underlying experimental claims are evaluated throughout OpenEval results.

Peer review expresses UNCERTAIN evaluation of CP temporal specificity claims (C19-C21, C24-C25), requesting additional validation that L1/L2 exposure has no effect. OpenEval does not separately evaluate these specific claims about larval stage effects, which are noted as based on unpublished data.
